does: Enriches and lightly thickens a hot sauce with egg yolks beaten with cream, without letting the yolks scramble.

intro.what: This method enriches a hot sauce with egg yolks beaten with cream.
intro.why: It teaches you to warm the yolks gradually and use gentle heat for a smooth, lightly thickened sauce.

how: Beat the yolks with the cream in a bowl.
Take the sauce off the boil.
Whisk a ladle of the hot sauce into the yolks to warm them, then another.
Pour the mixture back into the pan, stirring all the time.
Heat gently, stirring, just until the sauce thickens a little. It must not boil again.

cues.text: The sauce turns ivory and velvety, and coats the spoon more thickly than before.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring the yolks straight into a boiling sauce, which sets them into threads.
mistakes.fix: Warm the yolks with a little hot sauce first.

mistakes.mistake: Boiling the sauce after the yolks have gone in.
mistakes.fix: Keep it below a simmer. A sauce that has started to grain can sometimes be rescued through a fine sieve.

quiz.question: What finish is the yolk and cream mixture meant to give?
choices: Separated threads of egg in liquid.
quiz.because: Yolks beaten with cream enrich and lightly thicken the sauce.

quiz.question: What happens before the yolk mixture returns to the pan?
choices: It is poured straight into a rolling boil.
It is cooked into firm pieces on its own.
Hot sauce is whisked into it gradually to warm it.
quiz.because: Adding hot sauce gradually warms the yolks before they meet the pan, helping avoid threads of set egg.

quiz.question: Which texture matches the intended result?
choices: A velvety sauce that coats the spoon more thickly.
A grainy sauce with separated liquid.
quiz.because: A velvety sauce coating the spoon more thickly shows the intended light thickening, rather than grainy or set yolk.

quiz.question: Yolks formed threads when added directly to boiling sauce. What would you change next time?
choices: Bring the sauce to a harder boil first.
Take the sauce off the boil and warm the yolks gradually with some sauce.
Stop stirring as soon as the yolks enter the pan.
quiz.because: Boiling sauce can set the yolks into threads. Take it off the boil and warm the yolks gradually before returning the mixture to gentle heat.

comes_after.why: It asks for the same judgment as a custard: yolks thickening a liquid just short of scrambling.
